title: Peace Time and its use in hospitals
summary: The Grammy-winning relaxation album with Ben Surman, played in hospitals, released through Koch/E1.

blocks.x: Then there’s a listing of several other projects. We could return to the Golden Beams catalogue…
We’d have to go into Music We Are.

And then of course, Peace Time. Peace Time was 2009. Now, Music We Are was recorded when? Because you’re showing on your discography the release date is 2011, but then there’s a clip on your website...

That’s what I thought. We just want to make sure the record’s straight if this is your website. But let’s talk about Peace Time because this is the one that garnered you the Grammy and that’s still in the New Age.

Peace Time. I again brought in Ben for that to enhance that. That used a flute sound and some sort of a sequenced piano pattern that Ben brought in and out, also some didgeridoo and other ambient sounds are on it. That actually (came about) through (an) association Lydia has with a woman, Jeanette… I’ll get the name. Was at one time a nurse at Kingston Hospital. The idea came up of collaborating. Her husband Chris is a musician (and) also did some relaxation music and there was a photographer in the area… I’ll come back down and get the names right, get it straight with Lydia so I’ll record it right. The point is that we hooked up with this Alaskan photographer and put the music to his still shots, which sort of rolled and moved. The music is being played in hospitals. Peace Time and Chris’ music also, along with this video for people who are maybe going to have an operation or whatever. In the room they can have headphones and listen to this music to soothe them. It’s also being used… played in the hospital for the staff to keep some kind of tranquility and gives them a vibe. So I’m really happy when people use this music in that context.
Yeah. To get a Grammy was also an extra treat for that. Ben and I both received Grammies for that, so that was greatly appreciated.
Was this a Golden Beams project that was distributed by eMusic?
No it was by Koch, which is now eMusic. It was Koch, now it’s E-1.
